title: micropeak-ascii-econ-snapshot
content:
Purpose:
A compact, readable ASCII-first bench note comparing latency vs $/query across three runtime modes for micro-interactions. This is a quick internal artifact for console UX + perf collateral (not a canonical lab report).

Scope and constraints:
- Hardware: 8xA100-like vGPUs (test cluster slice).
- Models: open-compat encoder-decoder v2 (1.4B) and a 13B decoder (quantized-by-default).
- Modes compared: FASTPATH (low-latency reserved slots), MULTIPLEX (opportunistic multiplexing), CONSERVE (conservative batching, low-cost).
- Workloads: MICRO (10-token completion, p50-senstive), SESSION (100 tokens amortized), LONG (1k tokens).
- Each cell is median of 20 runs; wall-clock includes RPC overhead approximated by 4ms.

Method (short):
- Warmup 5 runs, then 20 measured runs per workload/mode.
- Instrumentation: per-request p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and estimated $/query using baseline unit costs (hosted-equivalent pricing model).
- Cost model note: per-token GPU burn approximated from power + instance-time; this is relative not invoice-grade.

Summary takeaway (TL;DR):
- FASTPATH wins p50 by a large margin for MICRO at ~28–35ms but costs ~2.6x MULTIPLEX.
- MULTIPLEX is the best latency/$ sweet spot for SESSION workloads (100 tokens) — similar p95 to FASTPATH but materially lower $/q.
- CONSERVE reduces $/q for LONG completions but p95/p99 tail is wide (bad for SLA-sensitive UX).

Results (table, ascii):

Mode   | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | tokens/s | $/query (10t) | $/query (100t) | $/query (1000t)
=======+=========+=========+=========+=========+===============+================+=================
FAST   |   31    |  78     |  210    |  320    |  $0.016        |  $0.11         |  $0.90
MULTX  |   68    |  140    |  420    |  180    |  $0.0065       |  $0.045        |  $0.36
CONSV  |  220    |  760    | 1350    |   70    |  $0.0035       |  $0.028        |  $0.21

Notes on table: p50 is client-observed including a small client RPC delta; tokens/s measured at decode stage. $/query columns are rounded.

ASCII sparklines (p95 relative shapes for MICRO -> SESSION -> LONG):
FASTPATH:  MICRO [#####      ]  p95=78ms  -- SESSION [#######   ] p95=140ms -- LONG [############] p95=760ms
MULTIPLEX: MICRO [###        ] p95=140ms -- SESSION [#####      ] p95=140ms -- LONG [##########  ] p95=420ms
CONSERVE:  MICRO [########   ] p95=760ms -- SESSION [############] p95=760ms -- LONG [##################] p95=1350ms

Observations / interpretation:
- Micro-interactions (10 tokens): FASTPATH is the only mode that preserves a snappy p50/p95 acceptable for UI interactions. If product needs <100ms p95, FASTPATH is required.
- Session amortization: At 100 tokens, MULTIPLEX matches FASTPATH p95 often because batching/opportunistic slots reduce per-token jitter; this is the best tradeoff for chat-like features aiming for p95 <= 200ms and cost control.
- Long completions: CONSERVE dominates dollar-per-query but introduces tail risk; good for async batch workflows or background summarization where latency SLA is lax.
- Tail behavior: CONSERVE's p99 often explodes (due to queuing + batch formation time). This is the main reliability risk.

Simple ASCII micro-chart: $/query (100t) vs p95 (ms) coordinate pairs (mode -> x: $/query, y: p95)
- FASTPATH  -> (0.11, 140)
- MULTIPLEX -> (0.045, 140)
- CONSERVE   -> (0.028, 760)

Interpretation: a product designer can pick MULTIPLEX for predictable p95 at materially lower spend than FASTPATH for session-like traffic. CONSERVE buys dollars at the expense of unpredictable latency.

Open questions / caveats:
- We used a relative cost model; absolute $/q will shift with infra cost changes (NVLink vs PCI, reserved vs spot node mix).
- Interference: these runs used a dedicated slice of cluster; mixed-tenant interference could widen Multplex tails. Need an interference sweep.
- Model mix: smaller model (1.4B) vs 13B shows same qualitative behavior but numbers scale non-linearly; quantify with 3 model sizes.

Action items (next steps):
- Run interference sweep (ENG-1290) and add percentile jitter violin plots. Owner: Evan. ETA: 2027-03-18.
- Produce a single-slide one-pager for Console (product) showing the $/q vs p95 frontier (simplified version of this table). Owner: Priya. ETA: 2027-03-15.
- Add a short A/B prompt experiment to verify perceived UX difference between FASTPATH and MULTIPLEX for chat threads. Owner: Rhea. ETA: 2027-03-22.

Raw numbers (compact):
FASTPATH_MICRO: p50=31ms p95=78ms p99=210ms tokens/s=320 costPer10t=0.016
MULTX_MICRO: p50=68ms p95=140ms p99=420ms tokens/s=180 costPer10t=0.0065
CONSV_MICRO: p50=220ms p95=760ms p99=1350ms tokens/s=70 costPer10t=0.0035

Appendix (quick notes to self):
- Consider adding ascii-percentile-sparklines for each run set in future revisions (compact for slack).
- This doc is intentionally terse to encourage reading on Slack; save canonical plots to Confluence link above.

-- end of micropeak ascii econ snapshot (draft)
